records.region: Southeastern Alaska and adjacent British Columbia; Chilkat Glacier setting, Chilkat River and Chilkat Inlet
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-system identity for the selected eastern Chilkat Glacier setting, ice-marginal foreland and upper Canadian receiving basin, continuous Chilkat River corridor and actual ending in Chilkat Inlet. This does not give the glacier, unnamed pool, tributaries or inlet a scalar river name.
records.completion_scope: Complete ordinary geographic correspondence for both selected mainstem fragments and all49 stored parts: chosen glacial opening, receiving foreland and upper basin, both international-border crossings, river junctions, braided and wetland river-bottom passages, estuary and actual render ending. The separate source endpoint is retained as terminal context. No exact-bank or present glacier-hydraulic claim is required or made.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-system identity for the selected eastern Chilkat Glacier setting, ice-marginal foreland and upper Canadian receiving basin, continuous Chilkat River corridor and actual ending in Chilkat Inlet. This does not give the glacier, unnamed pool, tributaries or inlet a scalar river name.

scope_limits: Representative system identity only. No single natural-river name is asserted for the whole selected glacier, unnamed pool/waterbody and marine-inlet composite.
No formal hydronym registry was verified; accepted, whole-feature scalar and Korean names remain null and application flags remain false.
The icefield name is bounded to the directly labeled broader Chilkat Glacier setting. No exact glacial-branch naming boundary, present meltwater route or subglacial connection is asserted.
Original topography and imagery depict different ice extents and have no common verified scene epoch. Ordinary connected topography/receiving geography is the assessment scale.
Selected positions are generalized orientation; no geometry correction, exact bank fitting, discharge, contemporary tidal shoreline or water-management operation is asserted.
The rendered ending and stored source endpoint are distinct. Both have the same bounded Chilkat Inlet receiving interpretation, and their coordinates are not republished.
Search-discovery snippets, unacquired reports and all inherited held originals/outputs supply no evidence.

records.region: Eastern Baffin Island, Nunavut: northern lake feeder, Generator Lake and Clyde River receiving corridor to the head of Kangiqtugaapik (Clyde Inlet).
records.geographic_disambiguation: Clyde River is the supported representative receiving-system name for the researched northern lake feeder, ice-margin lake passage and northeastern receiving river. Regulatory geographic prose names its connection to Generator Lake and independently edited CHS prose names its inlet-head mouth. Continuous ordinary photographic correspondence joins those contexts to every selected component. This does not rename the unnamed northern feeder, the individual lakes, Barnes Ice Cap or Kangiqtugaapik as Clyde River.
records.completion_scope: Clyde River is supported as the representative receiving-system candidate. All28 selected parts are accounted for: the small northern opening lake and southwest feeder, confined lake chain beside the ice-margin terrain, the selected Generator Lake passage, eastward outlet, northeast river and tributary joins, and the inlet-head delta/coastal ending. The source and rendered terminals are separately described. No official registry verification or name application is performed.
records.supported_name_scope: Clyde River is the supported representative receiving-system name for the researched northern lake feeder, ice-margin lake passage and northeastern receiving river. Regulatory geographic prose names its connection to Generator Lake and independently edited CHS prose names its inlet-head mouth. Continuous ordinary photographic correspondence joins those contexts to every selected component. This does not rename the unnamed northern feeder, the individual lakes, Barnes Ice Cap or Kangiqtugaapik as Clyde River.

scope_limits: Formal registry verification is unperformed. No accepted scalar name, Korean name or automatic application is supplied.
Clyde River is a receiving-system identity; no separate name is established for the chosen northern feeder, its small lakes or each joining stream.
The pinned rendered length is inventory context, not an independently surveyed river length.
Ordinary correspondence does not require exact agreement with every coarse selected vertex or proof of present water flow, tidal state or glacier hydraulics.
The separate source and rendered endpoints lie in the same inlet-head delta/coastal setting. They are not asserted to be surveyed present-day mouth vertices.

records.region: Northern Patagonia, Río Negro, Argentina: interior northern feeder and dry-valley sequence entering Laguna Carri-Laufquen Grande.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The successfully inspected report names the receiving lake and separately identifies the southern Maquinchao/Huahuel Niyeo approach, while describing important inflows from the north without naming this selected feeder. The photographic originals supply complete geographic correspondence but no hydronym. No supported representative natural-river name for the whole selected northern route is established.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected northern feeder, successive canyon and alluvial corridors, and terminal lakebed have complete ordinary geographic correspondence. The receiving-lake name is supported, but neither it nor separately named southern rivers is a representative natural-river name for this selected northern route.
records.completion_scope: Three overlapping original photographic views cover every stored part and intervening join from the chosen northern opening through an eastward valley and southward/southwestward canyon sequence into the Grande receiving basin. The lower view and DPA historical processed-lake imagery establish the continuous alluvial-to-lakebed passage and actual ending. A presently wet thread, exact banks and a blue line across every dry patch are unnecessary for this ordinary geographic correspondence.
records.supported_name_scope: The selected northern feeder, successive canyon and alluvial corridors, and terminal lakebed have complete ordinary geographic correspondence. The receiving-lake name is supported, but neither it nor separately named southern rivers is a representative natural-river name for this selected northern route.

scope_limits: No official river-name registry, representative natural-river hydronym, true river alias or Korean name is established for the selection.
The 2012 report and multitemporal photographic mosaic are not evidence of present surface flow, lake level, exact bank positions or contemporary water-management operation.

The report describes small closed depressions within the larger basin. The finding does not infer throughflow merely from basin membership: the selected canyon, alluvial and lakebed receiving corridors were inspected directly.
Scattered cloud and shadow patches locally reduce photographic detail but do not hide a material selected receiving corridor or require an unobserved interbasin transfer.
The report includes a regional longitude typographical inconsistency in its Maquinchao prose. That coordinate is not used as a location anchor.
A completed geographic result does not clear any inherited optional-source acquisition or unresolved publication-identity hold.

records.region: Interior lake-and-river corridor southwest of Postville, Labrador, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Completed geographic correspondence, with an unresolved selected-outlet naming assignment. Regional occurrence of Kaipokok River and the similarly named bay is not enough to rename the researched composite. No lake, tributary or upper branch name is inferred from snippets, the model, or imagery.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Four sequential, successfully acquired and visually read imagery views establish ordinary correspondence from the chosen western pond-and-lake chain, around its northward turn, through a long upper lake, winding receiving valleys and the major southern tributary join, through the two elongate lower lake basins and their interconnections, to the actual inner-bay ending. Independently read coastal prose locates the Kaipokok Bay setting, while modern field-project prose attests Kaipokok River and English River near Postville. These sources do not securely assign Kaipokok River to this exact selected receiving outlet. The geographic work is complete; the representative name stays null.
records.completion_scope: All33 stored parts in the one stage3 mainstem fragment were researched. The geographic stopping condition is met after the detailed western lake-chain connection was inspected. The primary state is a completed null-name scope hold, not a source-material-pending through-link gap. Optional and inherited source restrictions remain in force.
records.supported_name_scope: Kaipokok River is regionally attested only; its assignment to the selected outlet remains unconfirmed.

scope_limits: Kaipokok River is a plausible regional identification lead but has not been securely placed on the selected outlet by the permitted sources actually read. No representative name is completed.

The connected upper and lower lakes and the joining tributaries have no separately supported names in this finding. Discovery-only Micmac, Warrens and branch-name references are not promoted to observations or candidate names.

Imagery contains local haze, scene seams and changing water colours. The opening detail and overlapping views nevertheless establish the ordinary receiving corridor; no same-date hydrological or water-colour interpretation is made.

This research does not establish exact banks, a currently wetted channel at every point, navigation conditions, lake salinity, current flow, legal hydronym status or a single scalar natural-river name for all selected lake and river components.
No selected glacier or managed reservoir passage is evident in the inspected imagery. This is bounded visual geography, not a comprehensive infrastructure or regulation inventory.

bounded_name_observations.name: Kaipokok Bay
bounded_name_observations.scope: The coastal setting is identified from ATL121 descriptions of the long southwestward bay and Postville, together with the independently read lower imagery. This bay name is not assigned as a river name.

bounded_name_observations.name: Kaipokok River
bounded_name_observations.scope: Contemporary Nunatsiavut Rivers Project prose and fieldwork captions use this river name near Postville. Exact selected-reach placement remains unconfirmed.

bounded_name_observations.name: English River
bounded_name_observations.scope: Tula distinguishes monitoring on Kaipokok and English rivers near Postville. No part of the selection is assigned the English River name.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
